messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty fired — INC-34567 (P1) — PRIVATE VPC control plane: KV cache degradation detected for multiple customers. Affected: AcmeCorp(vpc-123), NimbusHealth(vpc-77), internal test fleets. Symptoms: increased control-plane read latency, cache miss storms, control plane error 502s. Playbook: https://confluence.redwood/ops/kvcache-ctrlplane-playbook 

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty -> INC-34567 assigned to Maya (oncall). Please ACK in 5m or escalation will trigger. Link: https://pd.redwood/INC-34567 

Maya (oncall): ack — I'm on it. pulling metrics, tagging SRE channel. starting triage. 

Jonah (sre): oncall handoff in 25m — if you need me sooner ping. can you paste relevant runbook step for cache degeneration? 

Maya (oncall): runbook extract -> Step 2: check cache hit ratio and eviction rate. Step 3: if sustained evictions > 20% for >60s, scale cache nodes and consider flush + warmup. see link above. grabbing redis stats now. 

Maya (oncall): logs/snippet: ```
# top controlplane kv metrics snapshot
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.42
kv_cache_evictions_per_min: 540
controlplane_read_latency_p95: 420ms
controlplane_errors_502: 74/min
```

Lisa (eng-runtime): I rolled a micro-optimization to kv eviction policy ~40m ago in canary; it's in canary group but might affect eviction churn under certain seq lengths. @Maya I can rollback that PR immediately if we think it's related. 

Maya (oncall): good catch. for immediate mitigation I'm going to scale kv nodes + enable read-through fallback to DB for affected controlplane pods. Will try flush to remove pathological entries after scaling. 

Customer Support: we've got two inbound tickets marked high from AcmeCorp and NimbusHealth — both report app errors and retries. Sending alert to their TAMs and opening a status update draft. Suggested short customer note: "We're investigating increased latency and errors with private control plane in your VPC. Engineers are working on mitigation; we'll follow up in 30 minutes." 

Maya (oncall): executing scale command now: ```
# scale controlplane-kv pool
kubectl scale --replicas=6 deploy/controlplane-kv-pool -n private-ctrlplane
``` 

pagerduty-bot: Acknowledge recorded by Maya (oncall). Escalation timer reset. If no progress in 10m, will escalate to PD Escalation. 

Maya (oncall): scaled + beginning cache warmup. issuing targeted flush on affected shard (shard-04) to clear pathological keys: ```
redis-cli -h kv-04.local -p 6379 --eval "FLUSHDB" 
``` Note: this will cause short spike in origin DB load. monitoring DB CPU. 

Jonah (sre): standing by to coordinate rollback. @Lisa if you think rollback to previous eviction policy is safer than flush, say so now. 

Lisa (eng-runtime): flush + scale first. if errors persist after warmup we'll rollback the micro-opt in canary and promote old policy. I'm queued to run rollback script if needed: ```
./deploy/rollback.sh --service controlplane-runtime --rev v1.42.7
``` 

Maya (oncall): metrics update (T+8m): hit_ratio -> 0.63, evictions -> 120/min, p95 latency -> 120ms, 502s -> 6/min. Customers still seeing reduced errors but intermittent. continuing to watch. :eyes: 

Customer Support: posted interim status to affected customers and to status.redwood.com (private notice). Customers acknowledged and asked for ETA; told them we'll follow up in 15m with next update. 

pagerduty-bot: No escalation needed — incident remains assigned to Maya (oncall). 

Maya (oncall): after 15m of warmup and monitoring, metrics stable. I'm going to keep the scaled pool for now and mark mitigation as active. planning to keep controlplane on reduced traffic for 30m then slowly ramp. 

Jonah (sre): I'll take the formal Handoff. @Maya if you want to step away, I'll own the incident for the next 40m and drive postmortem. Checklist: preserve logs, capture flamegraphs, run cache key distribution analysis. 

Maya (oncall): handing off to Jonah. my notes: suspected root cause = eviction churn due to recent eviction-policy micro-opt interacting with long-sequence keys in some private VPC workloads. Mitigation = scale kv pool, targeted flush, enable read-through fallback. No data loss observed. PD link: https://pd.redwood/INC-34567 

Jonah (sre): ack handoff — I'm on. creating incident channel for postmortem and action items: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/INC-34567-postmortem. Assigning followups: rollback verification (Lisa), telemetry improvement (Maya), customer comms followup (Customer Support). 

PD Escalation: Escalation not needed — incident stabilized. Please ensure runbook updated to include eviction churn checks and canary gating for eviction-policy changes. 

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED at 2723457389 UTC — control plane KV cache metrics returned to baseline after scaling and targeted flush. Root cause suspected as eviction-policy change interacting with certain private workloads. Action items assigned in postmortem page. Please fill the postmortem template within 48 hours. :white_check_mark:

Maya (oncall): thanks team — marking this thread closed from oncall side. I'll attach the quick graphs and raw logs to the confluence postmortem in a bit. 

Lisa (eng-runtime): will queue the rollback verification and add a tighter canary gate for eviction metrics. 

Customer Support: will follow up with customers and provide a timeline for impact/resolution. 

Jonah (sre): closing the incident. followups scheduled.
